solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Bad attitude, say, during Christmas scene

indicators.note: something happening during an event sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: the nativity scene depicts the birth of Jesus at Christmas
'say' introduces an example, abbreviated e.g.

explanation.surface: Someone sulking grumpily through the family's Christmas festivities.
explanation.walkthrough: NATIVITY holds EG to give NEGATIVITY.
explanation.definitionFit: Negativity is a pessimistic, unhelpful outlook, which counts as a poor frame of mind.

clue.text: Harry Potter in film’s premiere creating revenue

indicators.note: to harry is to harass and disturb, so these letters get pushed out of their order
a premiere is a first showing, so only the opening letter of the word is wanted

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
the first letter of film

explanation.surface: A Harry Potter film opening makes a fortune at the box office.
explanation.walkthrough: Harry Potter reads as the boy wizard, but Harry is the anagram signal working on Potter.
explanation.definitionFit: Net profit is the income a business keeps after costs, a loose sense of earnings or takings.

clue.text: Golden Age Hollywood actress to tear tabloid up

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading the letters from bottom to top, backwards

blocks.note: to rend is to tear apart
a rag is a disparaging word for a cheap newspaper

explanation.surface: A furious star rips up the gossip paper that slandered her.
explanation.walkthrough: RENDRAG read upwards gives GARDNER.
explanation.definitionFit: Ava Gardner was a leading MGM film star of the 1940s and 1950s, Hollywood's classic studio era.

clue.text: Brushing off one good impediment to marriage proposal?

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
G is the standard abbreviation for good
a suitor with no ring is hampered when proposing; the question mark flags this playful reading

explanation.surface: Someone dismissing a single obstacle that stands in the way of a wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: I + G + NO RING gives IGNORING.
explanation.definitionFit: Brushing someone off means deliberately disregarding them and paying them no attention.

clue.text: Staff admitted to wearing priestly garments in capitalist organisations

indicators.note: something admitted is let inside, so this piece goes into the other

blocks.note: dressed in something means wearing it
vestments are the robes worn by clergy
a club is a heavy stick, a kind of staff

explanation.surface: A cleric's staff is let into a gathering of people in priestly robes.
explanation.walkthrough: The staff slips in just before the final letter of the garments, so the plural ending stays at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Investment clubs are groups who pool money to buy shares, so they are bodies built around capital and profit.

clue.text: Comment made when contemptuous lout grabs bishop

indicators.note: grabbing something means holding it, so one piece is held within the other

blocks.note: a yahoo is a coarse, boorish person
B is the chess notation for bishop

explanation.surface: A sneering thug seizes a churchman and jeers at him.
explanation.walkthrough: YAHOO holds B to give YAHBOO.
explanation.definitionFit: Yah-boo is a British jeering interjection, the derisive noise of schoolyard mockery and scorn.

clue.text: Letters penned by dilettante, a lazy dabbler

indicators.note: letters penned by some words are enclosed within them, so the run of letters sits inside the phrase

blocks.note: the run spans the end of the first word, the a, and the start of the last

explanation.surface: An idle amateur jotting down letters with little effort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dabbler' looks like a description of the dilettante, but it is the definition: a teal is a dabbling duck.
explanation.definitionFit: Teal are dabbling ducks, which feed by tipping forward at the surface rather than diving.

clue.text: Finally get hold of dog with fluffy hair

blocks.note: to dog someone is to follow or trail them
down is fine soft hair or feathers

explanation.surface: At last catching a fluffy-coated dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dog' reads as a pet, but here it is a verb meaning follow.
explanation.definitionFit: To track down is to locate after searching, catching someone or something in the end.

clue.text: Italian merchant‘s donation, wanting day off

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so a letter is removed from the word
off means gone wrong or out of order, so the remaining letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
D is the abbreviation for day

explanation.surface: An Italian trader's gift misses the day it was due.
explanation.walkthrough: DONATION loses D, and the remaining ONATION is rearranged into ANTONIO.
explanation.definitionFit: Antonio is the title character of Shakespeare's The Merchant of Venice, set in Italy.

clue.text: Novelist‘s desperate, lacking time and energy to break into television

indicators.note: lacking means without, so a letter is removed
breaking into something means getting inside it, so these letters go within the other piece

blocks.note: an urgent need is a desperate one
T is the abbreviation for time
E is the symbol for energy in physics
TV is the standard abbreviation for television

explanation.surface: A writer is frantic to get onto television but has no time or energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'And energy' adds a letter after the one taken away, before everything goes inside television's abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivan Turgenev was the nineteenth-century Russian author of Fathers and Sons.

clue.text: Ambassador having pretentious tendencies is jovial

blocks.note: His Excellency, the title of an ambassador, is abbreviated HE
arty describes someone affecting artistic sophistication

explanation.surface: A pompous diplomat with artistic airs turns out to be good company.
explanation.walkthrough: HE + ARTY gives HEARTY.
explanation.definitionFit: Hearty describes a loud, cheerful, warmly enthusiastic manner, much like jolly or genial.

clue.text: Where to get a taxi from station

blocks.note: first meaning: a place where cabs queue for passengers
second meaning: position or standing in society

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a cab outside a railway station, but station here means social standing.
explanation.definitionFit: A taxi rank is where cabs wait in line, and rank also means one's grade or status in a hierarchy.

clue.text: After selling out, what shopkeeper’s doing about legwear

definitions.text: After selling out, what shopkeeper’s doing

blocks.note: re is Latin-derived for concerning or about
a stocking is a garment for the leg

explanation.surface: A shop that has sold out of hosiery needs more.
explanation.walkthrough: RE + STOCKING gives RESTOCKING.
explanation.definitionFit: Once goods are gone, a trader refills the shelves with fresh supplies of merchandise.

clue.text: Handle isn’t working with frame

indicators.note: working implies being processed or worked over, so these letters are reshaped

blocks.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped
taken as written

explanation.surface: A broken handle is not working, frame and all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Handle' suggests a door fitting, but it is slang for a name.
explanation.definitionFit: Handle is informal slang for the name a person goes by, such as a given name.

clue.text: Austrians spent this start of September relaxing

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, so only that is taken

blocks.note: the first letter of September
chilling is slang for relaxing

explanation.surface: Austrian tourists taking it easy in early autumn, spending freely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spent' reads as passing time, but it means spent money.
explanation.definitionFit: The schilling was Austria's currency until the euro replaced it in 2002.

clue.text: Bust — or the opposite overwhelming society

indicators.note: overwhelming something engulfs it, so one piece swallows the other

blocks.note: boom is the reverse of bust in economic cycles
S is an abbreviation for society

explanation.surface: A market crash, or its reverse, swamping high society.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bust' is both the definition (a chest) and the economic sense whose opposite, BOOM, holds S.
explanation.definitionFit: Bosom and bust both mean a woman's chest, the front of the upper body.

clue.text: Maybe Brummie lad badly nursed by nanny

indicators.note: badly means not done right, so the letters come out jumbled
a nurse holds a child, so one piece is held inside the other

blocks.note: the letters of lad, rearranged
a minder looks after children, as a nanny does

explanation.surface: A Birmingham boy being clumsily cared for by his nanny.
explanation.walkthrough: MINDER holds a rearranged LAD as MI-DLA-NDER. A Brummie is someone from Birmingham, England's second city.
explanation.definitionFit: Birmingham lies in the English Midlands, so a Brummie is one example of someone from that region.

clue.text: Dwell to the north, welcoming fix for part of entrance

indicators.note: in a down clue, heading north means reading the letters upwards, backwards
welcoming a guest means taking them in, so one piece goes inside

blocks.note: to brood is to dwell on something gloomily
a jam is a fix, a tight spot

explanation.surface: Someone living up north invites a builder to mend the front door.
explanation.walkthrough: BROOD reversed is DOORB, which takes in JAM.
explanation.definitionFit: A doorjamb is the vertical post forming each side of a doorframe.

clue.text: Close game that’s without odds?

indicators.note: dropping the odd-numbered letters leaves only the even ones

blocks.note: tig is the playground chasing game, also called tag
the second and fourth letters

explanation.surface: A sporting contest so evenly matched that no bookmaker offers odds.
explanation.walkthrough: TIG + HT gives TIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: A tight finish or contest is a close one, decided by a narrow margin.

clue.text: Sign snobs flee without clothing, which is unseemly

indicators.note: stripped of clothing means the outer letters come off, leaving only the inside

blocks.note: sign without its outer letters
snobs without its outer letters
flee without its outer letters

explanation.surface: A notice warning that snobs run away naked, which is hardly decent.
explanation.walkthrough: IG + NOB + LE gives IGNOBLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ignoble describes conduct that is dishonourable and base, so improper and unbecoming.

clue.text: In Le Monde, a determined journo is without proof

blocks.note: un is French for a, as a French paper would print it
found as in established or ruled by a court
ED is short for editor

explanation.surface: A dogged reporter at Le Monde finds his story has no evidence.
explanation.walkthrough: Le Monde is a French newspaper, so a is the French UN; UN + FOUND + ED gives UNFOUNDED.
explanation.definitionFit: An unfounded claim has no basis in fact, lacking evidence or support.

clue.text: Nothing new in flipping commercial shopping centre

indicators.note: flipping something turns it over, so this word is read backwards
in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: an ad is a commercial
N is the abbreviation for new
a mall is a shopping centre

explanation.surface: Nothing fresh in that wretched advert for the shopping centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' reads as a mild British curse, as in 'flipping heck', but it is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Damn all is British slang for absolutely nothing at all.

clue.text: Concerned with this lady’s adversary turning up

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the letters run upwards, backwards

blocks.note: the lady's things are hers, possessive her
a foe is an enemy or adversary

explanation.surface: Worried that this woman's enemy has shown up.
explanation.walkthrough: HER + FOE reversed gives HEREOF.
explanation.definitionFit: Hereof is a formal legal word meaning of or about this document or matter.

clue.text: E.g. TikTok star is awfully cruel, not primarily fine

indicators.note: awfully suggests something done terribly, so the letters come out mangled
primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter is taken

blocks.note: taken as written
the first letter of not
taken as written

explanation.surface: A social media celebrity is nasty and not really fine at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not primarily fine' looks like a phrase meaning not quite fine; it gives N plus FINE.
explanation.definitionFit: An influencer is a social media personality paid to sway followers, and TikTok is a major platform for them.

clue.text: Madame Bovary is a classic novel

blocks.note: first meaning: Flaubert's heroine, by her first name
second meaning: Jane Austen's 1815 book

explanation.walkthrough: The surface says Madame Bovary is a classic novel, which is true; the answer is the heroine's first name and a different classic.
explanation.definitionFit: Flaubert's heroine is called Emma Bovary, and Emma is also the title of a famous Austen book.

clue.text: Force old banks in Berne to save 51 thousand pounds

indicators.note: the banks of something are its edges, so only the outer letters are kept
saving something keeps it safe inside, so one piece holds the other

blocks.note: O is the abbreviation for old
the outer letters of Berne
LI is 51 in Roman numerals
G stands for a grand, a thousand pounds

explanation.surface: Swiss banks in Berne pressed to keep a large sum of money safe.
explanation.walkthrough: Banks of a river are its edges; G for a grand is slang for a thousand pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: To oblige someone is to compel or require them to act, legally or morally.

clue.text: Doughty United supporter backing attack

indicators.note: backing means moving backwards, so this word is read the other way

blocks.note: U is the abbreviation for United in team names
a fan supports a team
a raid is a sudden attack

explanation.surface: A brave football fan cheering on the attacking players.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing' reads as supporting, but it reverses FAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Doughty is an old-fashioned word for brave and resolute, so fearless or bold.

clue.text: The main hazard for an experimental composer

blocks.note: first meaning: short for iceberg, a danger at sea, the main being the ocean
second meaning: Alban ..., the Austrian atonal modernist

explanation.walkthrough: 'The main hazard' reads as the chief danger, but the main is the sea in crossword language.
explanation.definitionFit: A berg is a floating iceberg threatening ships, and Alban Berg wrote innovative twelve-tone music like Wozzeck.

clue.text: One providing rapid delivery of dish received by person who won’t eat it?

indicators.note: something received by a person is taken in, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: someone fasting refuses food
a bowl is a dish

explanation.surface: A quick food delivery handed to someone who is fasting.
explanation.walkthrough: FASTER holds BOWL. In cricket the bowler delivers the ball, so a fast bowler bowls at high speed.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a delivery is a single ball bowled, and this player sends it down at speed.
